prompt:
Intended use: a production candidate for ONE continuous 16-frame sword attack animation in an original guofeng cartoon browser game. Edit Image 1, the supplied 2816x2816 reference canvas, into a complete 4 COLUMN by 4 ROW spritesheet. It is a row-major temporal sequence, left to right on each row, then next row. EXACTLY sixteen equal 704x704 cells. Each cell contains ONE full-body pose of THE SAME approved adult swordsman shown in the top-left cell. This is NOT a collection of unrelated action illustrations and NOT four key poses repeated. Every successive cell is the next small motion step, sixteen genuine animation poses for 24 FPS playback, lasting about two thirds of a second.

Identity and drawing invariants: preserve his adult face and angular chin, long dark half-up hair and small topknot, white and warm-gray robe with pale jade-green edging and the same cloud motifs, charcoal inner clothes, red waist cord and red wrist wraps, dark jade boots, straight silver Chinese sword with an ornate muted-brass guard and red tassel. Same costume, same head size, same limb proportions, same one sword and two hands, same confident-but-nervous dryly comic expression. Original animation-style guofeng with clean expressive contour lines, readable color groups and limited cel shadows. No photorealistic cloth or skin texture. Do not change him to a child, chibi mascot, different character or existing franchise. Preserve the reference's right-facing three-quarter side view, camera angle and lighting throughout.

Layout: flat perfectly uniform bright magenta #FF00FF background ONLY, including all gutters. No transparent checkerboard. Invisible cell boundaries at multiples of 704 pixels; do not draw any lines, numbers, frame labels, lettering or diagram arrows. Keep complete hair, hands, both boots, robe tails and sword tip INSIDE their respective cells, with at least 32 pixels of magenta clearance to every cell boundary. Use one consistent body scale and a common floor position near y=656 in each cell. The head-to-boot standing height is about 560 pixels in every upright pose; crouching changes actual silhouette but must not resize the anatomy. No part of a pose may spill into its neighbour. Two anatomical legs and two boots in every frame, never extra arms, detached fingers, duplicated blades or additional people. Plain cutout assets, no scenery, ground shadow, floor, sparks, magic trail, motion blur or VFX; effects will be composited separately by the engine.

Motion choreography, SIXTEEN successive small steps rather than four disconnected drawings: cell 1 is the approved ready stance, sword lowered diagonally toward the right. Cell 2 softens the knees and begins a modest shoulder turn. Cell 3 brings the sword hand inward while the blade tip rises. Cell 4 coils torso and lifts the sword behind the shoulder. Cell 5 completes the raised anticipation with the off hand balanced near the chest. Cell 6 starts the forward weight shift and uncoils the shoulder. Cell 7 continues forward, blade passing above and in front of the head. Cell 8 is the middle of a controlled diagonal downward cut, wrist and elbow moving smoothly. Cell 9 continues the SAME cut toward the right, blade crossing the forward chest area. Cell 10 reaches the forward extension, clear complete sword and stable knees. Cell 11 follows through slightly lower, robe hem and red tassel following the motion. Cell 12 absorbs the momentum, elbow starting to bend. Cell 13 draws the sword hand back with a small torso recoil. Cell 14 straightens toward the ready stance, robe still settling. Cell 15 eases the blade down with the off hand returning to the reference position. Cell 16 is a near-reference recovery stance, weight settled and blade low, allowing a clean return to idle. Spatial motion must be gradual across row boundaries as well as within rows. No teleporting pose, sudden facing reversal, abrupt size changes or sword swapping hands. The grounded feet may flex and shift modestly but never slide off the shared baseline. Preserve the supplied seed in the first frame's identity and proportions. Prioritize readable continuous timing, clean anatomy and exact sixteen-cell packing.
